sn12.1:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Savatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anathapiṇḍika’s Park.
sn12.1:1.3: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn12.1:1.7: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you dependent origination.
sn12.1:1.8: Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.”–
sn12.1:2.2: With ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be;
sn12.1:2.3: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness;
sn12.1:2.5: with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases;
sn12.1:2.6: with the six sense bases as condition, contact;
sn12.1:2.12: with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.
sn12.1:2.13: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.1:2.14: This, bhikkhus, is called dependent origination.
sn12.1:3.1: “But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations; with the cessation of volitional formations,
sn12.1:3.3: with the cessation of consciousness, cessation of name-and-form;
sn12.1:3.4: with the cessation of name-and-form, cessation of the six sense bases;
sn12.1:3.5: with the cessation of the six sense bases, cessation of contact;
sn12.1:3.6: with the cessation of contact, cessation of feeling;
sn12.1:3.7: with the cessation of feeling, cessation of craving;
sn12.1:3.8: with the cessation of craving, cessation of clinging;
sn12.1:3.9: with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence;
sn12.1:3.10: with the cessation of existence, cessation of birth;
sn12.1:3.11: with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.
sn12.1:3.12: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
sn12.1:3.13: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn12.1:3.14: Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.
